## [What Diffraction Actually Is, and Why Photographers Worry About f/16](https://fstoppers.com/education/what-diffraction-actually-and-why-photographers-worry-about-f16-904091?utm_source=fstoppers&utm_medium=RSS&utm_campaign=rss_feed_articles)
*Fstoppers* | 03/10/2026 | Score: 0.74
Tags: photography, lens

> A 24mm lens at f/8 has an opening 3.00 mm across. A 600mm lens at f/8 has one 75 mm across, 25 times wider, and it draws a diffraction pattern on the sky 25 times finer. Both land a blur spot on your sensor exactly 10.7 microns wide. Every other limit in photography has a price attached. Aberrations yield to better glass, noise yields to a bigger sensor, flare yields to better coatings. Diffraction yields to nothing, because it is not a property of your lens at all. [ Read More ]
